entries.title: High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution
entries.description: The AIDS epidemic could stage a comeback amid unequal access to breakthrough prevention medicines and a sharp decline in global funding, according to a UN report released on Monday ahead of the opening of the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

entries.title: WHO warns DR Congo Ebola outbreak is outpacing response as Uganda reaches milestone
entries.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the third largest on record and is spreading faster than any previous one during the first month of exposure, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday.

entries.title: WHO: Integration, innovation and community leadership key to ending HIV, hepatitis and STIs
entries.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) today launched a new report assessing progress in implementing the Global Health Sector Strategies (GHSS) on HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) for 2022–2030. Released during the 26th International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) and ahead of World Hepatitis Day (28 July), the report highlights significant achievements and persistent challenges in the global response to these epidemics.

entries.title: WHO launches seven strategies to prevent drowning
entries.description: Ahead of World Drowning Prevention Day on 25 July, the World Health Organization (WHO) is launching a new technical package to help governments and communities implement seven proven measures to reduce drowning deaths.

entries.title: UN report: Global hunger levels ease for third consecutive year as regional disparities persist
entries.description: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025, demonstrating that progress is possible. However, the improvements remain fragile, unevenly distributed and insufficient to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, according to The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026 (SOFI 2026) report, released on Tuesday by five United Nations specialized agencies.

entries.title: Road deaths fall by 21% globally but stronger action is needed to save lives
entries.description: Despite the addition of more than one billion motor-vehicles to the world’s roads, road traffic deaths declined by 21% between 2011 and 2025, according to new data released by the World Health Organization (WHO). The world has experienced profound changes in road traffic during this time with the emergence of new modes of transport and a sharp rise in motorcycle use. Despite this progress, however, road traffic crashes still claimed 1.16 million people's lives in 2025. Road traffic injuries remain the leading cause of death among children and youth aged 5–29 years. The new WHO data comes as gl

entries.title: WHO marks 25 years of Research4Life, advancing access to scientific knowledge in more than 120 countries
entries.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) today marks the 25th anniversary of Research4Life, a public-private partnership that provides researchers, educators, health professionals and policy-makers in low- and middle-income countries with affordable or free access to scientific knowledge. The partnership has helped dramatically expand access to scientific knowledge for researchers, educators, health professionals and policy-makers in more than 120 countries.

entries.title: [Articles] Efficacy and safety of tirofiban after successful endovascular reperfusion in acute ischaemic stroke (ATTRACTION) in China: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
entries.description: In patients with acute ischaemic stroke due to anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion achieving successful reperfusion, adjunctive tirofiban increased the likelihood of functional independence compared with placebo. Although symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage occurred numerically more often with tirofiban, the between-group difference was not significant, and this finding warrants caution when weighing potential benefit against bleeding risk.

entries.title: Cyberattacks and the digital divide are creating new barriers to HIV services
entries.description: Cyberattacks, data breaches, online harassment and other forms of technology-facilitated violence are becoming significant obstacles to HIV prevention and treatment, according to a UNAIDS specialist who says digital security has become inseparable from the fight against the epidemic itself.

entries.title: WHO adds first diagnostic test for Ebola Bundibugyo virus to its Emergency Use Listing
entries.description: Today, the World Health Organization (WHO) has added the first molecular diagnostic test for Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) to its Emergency Use Listing (EUL). The test detects the virus by identifying its genetic material in blood samples, helping confirm infection rapidly and accurately. WHO’s EUL procedure assesses the quality, safety and performance of essential health products based on the available evidence, while ensuring they meet minimum international standards and address the needs of low- and middle-income countries. Through this mechanism, WHO aims to accelerate access to reliable diagnos

entries.title: Wildfires surge across Europe as Spain and France battle major blazes
entries.description: The amount of land burned by wildfires across Europe has increased by 57 per cent in four years, according to new data from the World Health Organization (WHO) in Europe.

entries.title: What the latest routine immunization coverage estimates mean for eradication
entries.description: The 2025 WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC), released last week, provide governments, donors, parents and health advocates with a comprehensive view of how well routine immunization systems are reaching children. For the Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI), the value of these numbers is in what it tells us about the strength of health […]

entries.title: Women football stars team up to kick polio out of Africa
entries.description: DAKAR, 22 July 2026 – Just days before the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) kicks off, African women footballers are calling on leaders across the continent to renew their political commitment, sustain investment and take collective action to protect every child from polio and other vaccine-preventable diseases. Launched by the Global Polio Eradication Initiative […]

entries.title: Science for the final mile: Researchers gather to shape the future of polio eradication
entries.description: For more than half a century, scientific discovery has helped protect millions of children from one of the world’s most feared diseases. Today, as the world stands closer than ever to eradicating polio, researchers continue to push the boundaries of innovation—not for the sake of science itself, but to ensure that every child, everywhere, can […]

entries.title: Polio simulation exercise strengthens system readiness to maintain Egypt’s polio-free status
entries.description: Egypt has maintained its polio-free status despite high and frequent population movement from polio-affected countries, a result of its strong routine immunization coverage and well-established surveillance system. To sustain this achievement requires continuous strengthening of early detection and rapid-response capacities. To support this, 68 technical staff from the Ministry of Health and Population, including participants […]

entries.title: Improved reporting needed on forest carbon emissions
entries.description: More analysis is needed to ensure that tropical forest degeneration and regeneration are consistently reported in carbon cycle models and in national reporting, according to a study funded in part by ESA's Climate Change Initiative Biomass project. The study analysed how tropical forests store carbon under varying conditions and then release it back into the atmosphere. entries.description: The UN General Assembly closed its first ever High-level Meeting on road safety on Tuesday by adopting a sweeping new declaration aimed at halving road deaths by 2030 – over the sole objection of the United States.

entries.title: ADB and Partners Power Timor-Leste’s Energy Future with Landmark Investment in Solar and Battery Storage
entries.description: ADB, the Government of Canada, the Japan International Cooperation Agency, and the World Bank Group have partnered to support Timor-Leste’s first utility-scale solar and battery storage project, accelerating the country’s energy transition, creating jobs, and supporting sustainable growth and prosperity.

entries.title: ADB Approves $160 Million Loan to Scale Up Bhutan’s Solar Power and Attract Private Investment
entries.description: ADB has approved a $160 million ordinary capital resources loan to scale up solar power generation in Bhutan. The project will deploy at least 310 megawatts of new solar generation capacity and attract private investment through the country's first private-majority public–private partnership in the energy sector.

entries.title: Inside the Race to Electrify Semitrailers for Long-Haul Freight
entries.description: A semitrailer that helps propel itself entered commercial road testing in late May, when a power-train kit developed by Nivalis Energy Europe, headquartered in Luxembourg with engineering operations in Germany, was fitted to a trailer supplied by the Amsterdam-based TIP Group. The self-powered trailer was handed over to the German transport operator Sommer for use in its working fleet. The Nivalis Powered Trailer Kit centers on an electric axle codeveloped with the running-gear specialist BPW, based in Wiehl, Germany. entries.title: Supercooled kidneys have been transplanted into pigs in a “landmark achievement”
entries.description: When it comes to organ donation, time is everything. As soon as an organ has been carefully removed from a donor’s body, it starts to deteriorate. Surgeons have a matter of hours to get it into a recipient. Leave it too long and the organ will become unusable. In most cases, organs will be kept…

entries.title: NASA's Perseverance just completed a marathon on Mars
entries.description: NASA's Perseverance rover has reached an impressive new milestone on Mars, completing the equivalent of a full marathon by driving 26.2 miles (42.195 kilometers) across the Red Planet. It accomplished the feat in just five years and four months, reaching the distance on its 1,890th Martian day, less than half the time it took the previous record holder, NASA's Opportunity rover.

entries.title: Tiny magnetic waves could unlock quantum computers the size of a penny
entries.description: A major breakthrough in quantum technology has turned magnons, tiny magnetic waves once considered too short-lived for practical use, into promising carriers of quantum information. Researchers extended their lifetime by nearly 100 times, reaching up to 18 microseconds, and discovered that the main limitation is not a law of physics but the purity of the material itself. That means future improvements could come from better manufacturing rather than entirely new discoveries.

entries.title: High-speed orcas are blowing sunfish to smithereens
entries.description: Never-before-seen behavior may represent the giant cetaceans playing with their food, ecologists say

entries.title: Odd shapes hidden in dense Amazon rainforest reveal sprawling ancient civilization
entries.description: Newly found earthworks suggest about 3 million people might have lived in just about 3% of the forest’s entire area

entries.title: Scientists create quantum sound device that could transform communications
entries.description: A new quantum device can generate precisely controlled bursts of sound-like particles, or phonons, by forcing electrons through an ultra-thin crystal at extremely low temperatures. The surprising behavior pushes beyond the limits predicted by current theories, suggesting scientists need to rethink how energy moves through advanced materials. In the future, the breakthrough could lead to phonon lasers, faster communications, improved medical technologies, and powerful new sensing systems.

entries.title: Clear sighting of ‘wandering’ black hole reveals escapee from galaxy merger

entries.title: British ‘First Fleet’ brought smallpox to Australia—and may have killed millions
entries.description: Two papers pin the deadly disease’s introduction on British colonists and suggest the continent held far more people than previously believed

entries.title: Knowledge Gatherer: Portrait of a Scientist's Wife in Victorian England
entries.description: When Dehn Gilmore, professor of English at Caltech, was investigating ideas for her next book, she had to look no further than her own family tree. As the great-great-granddaughter of German-born British scientist Sir Arthur Schuster—a Victorian-era physicist who coined the term "antimatter," popularized the X-ray in England, and built one of the largest physics labs in the world, among other achievements—she wanted to know more about the scientist in her lineage and his similarly successful siblings.Her forthcoming book, which will publish in 2027, offers a panoramic account of Britain's cult

entries.title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing
entries.description: The visionary PhysioNet platform launched 25 years ago, based on a system developed at MIT in the 1970s. It has become one of the most comprehensive biomedical and clinical data repositories in existence.

entries.title: MIT and Broad Institute researchers break diffraction barrier in super-resolution microscopy
entries.description: New U-STORM imaging technology lets scientists view molecular structures in subatomic detail — about 1,000 times clearer than traditional dyes — while making the microscope process much simpler.

entries.title: A tiny molecular basket unlocks a powerful new kind of chemistry
entries.description: Rice University chemists have found a new way to make neodymium, a rare-earth metal, interact with oxygen. Using a specially designed molecular structure described as a “basket,” the team positioned the atoms so they could form a bond once thought unlikely. The breakthrough produced highly reactive compounds that could eventually give chemists alternatives to iron-based molecules used in biological reactions and chemical manufacturing.

entries.title: IEEE Publishing Ethics Team Upholds Research Integrity
entries.description: Given a rising number of publishing misconduct allegations, IEEE in 2022 created the Publishing Ethics Team as a centralized department to assist in handling claims. The group also works to increase the organization’s visibility in the broader publishing ethics area and helps IEEE volunteers write new policies. Here are some highlights of the team’s activities last year. entries.title: Ancient Stardust Were Seeds for the Earliest Solids in the Solar System
entries.description: How did the first solids that made up planets, moons, and asteroids form out of the "hot soup" that characterized our solar system's earliest years? entries.description: MIT-trained mathematicians earn the honor, one of the most prestigious in the field, for their significant achievements.

entries.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with men’s soccer captain Dilin Meloni
entries.description: The rising senior is passionate about soccer, nuclear fusion, and advocating on behalf of his fellow student-athletes at MIT.

entries.title: MIT Professor Susumu Tonegawa, renowned molecular biologist and Nobel laureate, dies at 86
entries.description: Tonegawa made landmark discoveries about how the immune system generates antibody diversity and how the brain forms memories.

entries.title: Ana Miljački named head of the Department of Architecture
entries.description: In this leadership role, Miljački seeks to shepherd a collective commitment to transform the present into a better future.

entries.description: The rise of automation and AI has raised fears about job loss, but a team led by Caltech medical engineers suggests that smart tools can help train and assist workers rather than replace them. The team has developed a low-cost device that trains and assists people with minimal laboratory experience to perform complex laboratory procedures. entries.title: Detect Dark Matter’s Mark From Your Backyard
entries.description: If you’re wondering what dark matter is, you’re not alone. Astronomers don’t know. But they’ve determined that this invisible material must be far more abundant than the stars and nebulas that they can see. They’ve surmised as much from observing the gravitational effects of all this perplexing dark stuff, launching a decades-long campaign to understand its nature. entries.description: Artificial intelligence is reshaping the skills employers expect from new graduates. In response, universities are scrambling to launch new courses, research centers, and industry partnerships that prepare students for today’s workforce. But building a cutting-edge AI curriculum demands funding and access to industry networks, resources that remain unevenly distributed across higher education. At North Carolina Central University, Siobahn Day Grady is trying to change that equation. entries.description: Physicists have been trying to measure the fundamental gravitational constant for well over two centuries. The current accepted value of big G, as it’s known, is 6.67430 × 10-11 cubic meters per kilogram per square second. It also has an uncertainty of ±0.00015 × 10-11 m3/(kg s2). entries.title: Garber warns of disruptions to ‘unprecedented’ scientific progress
entries.description: Policy changes for research funding, international students threaten U.S. momentum, he says

entries.title: America at 250: What UC Berkeley historians want us to remember
entries.description: Hidetaka Hirota, Brian DeLay and David Henkin explain how the nation has transformed since 1776 and remind us that American history stretches back even further than the Revolution. The post America at 250: What UC Berkeley historians want us to remember appeared first on Berkeley News.

entries.title: Scientists create an “electron lighthouse” with laser light
entries.description: Scientists have created an “electron lighthouse” that uses laser light to launch and steer electrons through a semiconductor without an applied electrical field. The quantum effect could eventually improve optical sensors, communications, imaging, and information storage.

entries.title: Inside the Backrooms: The internet’s creepiest place is becoming a tourist attraction
entries.description: The Backrooms began as a single eerie image of empty yellow rooms, but internet users transformed it into a vast fictional world that feels disturbingly real. Through videos, games, maps, survival guides and social media stories, audiences do more than watch the horror unfold. They help build and explore it. Researchers suggest this popularity reflects a new kind of digital tourism, where people emotionally enter imaginary places filled with mystery, nostalgia and unease.

entries.title: NASA selects four new Moon missions to build a permanent lunar base
entries.description: NASA is ramping up its lunar ambitions by awarding nearly $600 million for four commercial Moon landings planned for late 2028. Each mission will carry the same trio of science instruments to improve lunar navigation, study dangerous dust kicked up during landings, and map the Moon's radiation environment. The agency also revealed plans for new rovers, communication satellites, and additional cargo missions as it lays the groundwork for a permanent Moon Base.

How might factors such as wind speed and direction, vegetation, and topology affect the fire's progression? Where are firefighting resources—both personnel and vehicles—located, and how much water and other necessary suppressants are available?In the wake of the Eaton Fire that devastated Altadena and parts of Pasadena in January 2025, researchers from Caltech recognized that technology has a role to play here. entries.title: NSF Funding for Caltech-Led "Cloud Laboratory" Leverages AI to Explore Chemical Dark Matter: A Conversation with Hosea Nelson
entries.description: Caltech chemistry professor Hosea Nelson (PhD '13) has his eyes on a big goal: He wants to know the three-dimensional (3D) structure of all the molecules found in the natural world. No one knows exactly how many structures that entails, but certainly, he says, it is at least millions. Those unknown structures make up what Nelson and others calls "chemical dark matter." entries.title: MIT projects selected for funding under US Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission
entries.description: Initial research projects advance national priorities across natural resources, manufacturing, nuclear physics, and more.

entries.title: Professor Emeritus Dimitri Bertsekas, influential computer scientist and prolific author, dies at 83
entries.description: Known for his clear and elegant writing style, Bertsekas shaped fields from control and optimization to large-scale computation and artificial intelligence.

entries.description: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans nuclear weapons in space, but there’s currently no way to verify that satellites aren’t carrying them.

entries.title: ADB Approves $182.89 Million Loan to Strengthen Public School System in Karnataka, India
entries.description: ADB has approved a $182.89 million (in yen equivalent) loan to help India strengthen the public school system in Karnataka, expanding access to high-quality learning and improving academic performance for more than a million students, including female and disadvantaged learners.

entries.title: ADB to Deploy $450 Million to Shield Cambodia, Sri Lanka from Middle East Impact
entries.description: ADB is set to deploy $450 million to protect poor households and strengthen the economies of Cambodia and Sri Lanka as the conflict in the Middle East drives up costs and deepens uncertainty across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB Supports Tbilisi Bypass with $250 Million Loan to Boost Georgia’s Regional Connectivity
entries.description: ADB has approved a $250 million loan to help build a critical bypass around Tbilisi that will improve road connectivity, ease congestion, and strengthen Georgia’s role as a regional transport hub in the region.

entries.title: ADB Approves $1 Billion Loan to Support Sustainable Growth and Resilience of India’s Cities
entries.description: ADB has approved a $1 billion loan to support the Government of India’s urban reform agenda by maintaining momentum of investment and reforms aimed at transforming cities into engines of economic growth, innovation, and livability.

entries.title: ADB Approves $850 Million Loan to Accelerate Affordable Rooftop Solar Adoption for Households in India
entries.description: ADB has approved an $850 million loan to support reforms that will speed up the rollout of the Government of India’s flagship rooftop solar program, boosting the resilience of Indian households through better access to affordable clean energy, mobilizing private sector investment, and strengthening the skills of grid personnel and rural entrepreneurs.

entries.title: ADB, Japan Establish New Water Security Fund
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Japan established a new fund to strengthen water security and protect people across Asia and the Pacific from worsening floods, droughts, and other water-related shocks. Japan will make an initial $10 million contribution to the fund.

entries.title: ADB Provides $2 Million Grant to Support Flood-Affected Communities in Thailand
entries.description: ADB has approved a $2 million grant to support the Government of Thailand as it expands humanitarian assistance for communities devastated by severe flooding in southern Thailand.

entries.title: ADB Approves $10 Million Grant to Strengthen Maritime Transport in Tuvalu
entries.description: ADB has approved a $10 million grant to help Tuvalu improve the operation and maintenance of ADB transport investments in the country, boosting maritime connectivity, trade, and economic development.

entries.title: ADB Approves $230 Million Loan to Modernize Water Supply and Sanitation in Chennai, India
entries.description: ADB has approved a $230 million loan to modernize and expand Chennai’s water supply and sanitation infrastructure, benefiting 4.5 million residents in the Greater Chennai area.

entries.title: ADB Approves $50 Million Loan to Modernize Nepal’s Customs, Boost Trade and Jobs
entries.description: ADB has approved a $50 million policy-based loan to help Nepal modernize its customs administration, boost trade, and support job creation.

entries.title: Global hunger declines again but progress remains uneven across regions
entries.description: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025 showing that progress is possible, but gains remain fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by the 2030 deadline.

entries.title: ‘Shared blueprint for peace’: Development goals deliver for billions, but challenges remain
entries.description: With fewer than five years left to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a new UN report says sustained investment and international cooperation have improved billions of lives, but warns that governments must urgently accelerate action if the goals are to be met by their 2030 deadline.

entries.title: ADB Puts Team on the Ground in Türkiye as Financing Demand Surges
entries.description: Recognizing Türkiye’s growing regional importance, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) will establish an office in the country as it prepares to commit about $3 billion a year to earthquake recovery, critical infrastructure, businesses, and trade routes linking Asia and Europe.

entries.title: ADB Loan Supports Stronger Earthquake Resilience at Schools in Armenia
entries.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Government of Armenia have signed a $293 million loan agreement to expand resilient, inclusive school infrastructure nationwide and strengthen the country's capacity to manage earthquake risks.

entries.title: Multilateral Development Banks Increase Climate Finance to Record $163 Billion in 2025, Supporting Resilient and Sustainable Growth
entries.description: MDBs increased climate finance to record levels in 2025, reinforcing their role in supporting resilient and sustainable economies.

entries.title: ADB, HDBank Sign $100 Million Loan to Expand Access to Finance for MSMEs, Women-Owned Businesses in Viet Nam
entries.description: ADB has signed a $100 million loan with Ho Chi Minh City Development Joint Stock Commercial Bank (HDBank) to expand access to finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Viet Nam, with a focus on women-owned MSMEs.

entries.title: ADB, Premium Nexus JSC Sign Social Loan to Promote Efficient and Inclusive Food Distribution in Mongolia
entries.description: ADB and Premium Nexus JSC have signed a $10 million (MNT35.8 billion equivalent) social loan to improve access to safe, affordable food and essential goods through modernized retail infrastructure, strengthened cold chain logistics, and expanded convenience store networks across Mongolia.

entries.title: ADB, Golomt Bank Partner to Expand Sustainable and Inclusive Finance in Mongolia
entries.description: ADB and Golomt Bank Joint Stock Company (Golomt Bank) have signed a $64 million loan agreement to support sustainable finance and expand lending to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including women-owned businesses in Mongolia.

entries.title: ADB Approves $70 Million Loan to Support Fiscal and Governance Reforms in the Kyrgyz Republic
entries.description: ADB has approved a $70 million concessional loan for subprogram 2 of the Sustainable Fiscal Management and Governance Improvement Program, supporting policy reforms to strengthen fiscal resilience, transparency, and public resource management in the Kyrgyz Republic.

entries.title: As aid dries up, countries pledge to close the $4 trillion development gap
entries.description: UN Member States reaffirmed their commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by adopting a declaration on Wednesday that they will implement reforms to help close the $4 trillion SDG financing gap.

entries.title: World News in Brief: Gaza aid challenges persist, renewed push for clean energy, Sudan cholera update
entries.description: Humanitarians in the Gaza Strip continue to face significant challenges in reaching communities located near the so-called “Yellow Line” in northern Rafah, the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Tuesday.

entries.title: Despite hurdles, don’t give up on Sustainable Development Goals, UN urges
entries.description: In a world of “parallel realities” where stark inequalities seemingly divide people and challenge the promise of multilateralism, the vision of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is to bring people together and help them achieve a better reality.

entries.title: ADB President Urges Faster Action on Water Security
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda has called for faster investment and reform to secure water across Asia and the Pacific, pointing to a new ADB-administered fund with Japan that will help developing economies strengthen disaster preparedness, infrastructure, and water management.

entries.title: ADB Launches Initiative to Bring Japanese Startup Innovation to Southeast Asia and the Pacific
entries.description: ADB and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have launched the Southeast Asia Emerging Entrepreneurs Kickstart initiative to help promising startups scale solutions to complex development challenges in Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB President Meets Nepal Prime Minister as Jobs and Investment Support is Stepped Up
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda met Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu as ADB and Nepal mark 60 years of partnership and deepen support for the country’s economic transformation, job creation, and investment.

entries.title: ADB Approves $12.5 Million Financing to Strengthen Fiscal Resilience and Sustainable Planning in Palau
entries.description: ADB has approved $12.5 million in concessional financing for the Republic of Palau to support reforms that strengthen public financial management, enhance resilience to extreme weather events, and promote sustainable economic development.

entries.title: ADB Establishes North Pacific Subregional Office, Expanding Support in Region
entries.description: ADB announced the establishment of a subregional office to support its expanding operations in the North Pacific, strengthening the bank’s commitment to its Pacific developing member countries as a steadfast partner for growth, development, and resilience.

entries.title: ADB Approves $200 Million Emergency Assistance for Sri Lanka’s Post-Cyclone Ditwah Recovery
entries.description: ADB has approved a $200 million emergency assistance package for Sri Lanka’s recovery and reconstruction following Cyclone Ditwah.

entries.title: ADB Approves $11 Million Grant to Boost Health Services In Kiribati
entries.description: ADB has approved an $11 million grant for health initiatives in Kiribati, highlighting the critical role the Asian Development Fund plays in supporting the country’s development priorities.

entries.title: ADB Approves $13 Million Financing for Resilient Urban Development in Bhutan
entries.description: ADB has approved a $13 million financing package to help the Government of Bhutan strengthen resilient urban infrastructure and expand affordable rental housing for low-income and vulnerable households, particularly in Thimphu and Phuentsholing.

entries.title: ADB, Converse Bank Sign $15 Million Financing to Boost Women-Owned MSMEs and Sustainable Lending in Armenia
entries.description: ADB has signed a financing package of up to $15 million with Converse Bank Closed Joint Stock Company to expand access to finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and households, and to support sustainable lending in Armenia.

entries.title: 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test
entries.description: As the world marks the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has launched a global campaign urging governments, organizations and individuals to renew their commitment to protecting people forced to flee war, violence and persecution.

entries.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
entries.description: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: International Criminal Court briefs on Darfur
entries.description: On Wednesday, the Security Council heard an update on the International Criminal Court's work in Sudan's Darfur region, referred to the Court back in 2005. Focus has recently turned to atrocities in the ongoing war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The briefing was held as the ICC faces mounting pressure: this week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a campaign to “dismantle” the Court, which prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and the crime of aggression. Follow full live coverage below.

entries.title: Peacekeepers step up support as families return to south Lebanon
entries.description: With violence in south Lebanon significantly decreased since mid-June, UN peacekeepers there have returned to core functions such as protecting humanitarian aid and restoring critical infrastructure as families continue to return home.

entries.title: West Africa and the Sahel: Terrorism is changing its face
entries.description: Jihadist groups are no longer content with launching attacks in West Africa and the Sahel: they administer territories, control trade routes, exploit new technologies and are gradually pushing their influence all the way to the Gulf of Guinea.

entries.title: World News in Brief: Aid deliveries to Gaza restricted, UN prepares El Nino response, El Salvador eliminates disease
entries.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is calling for greater humanitarian access to Gaza, warning that restrictions on aid deliveries, ongoing violence and funding shortages are severely limiting its ability to reach people in need.

entries.title: How might AI transform science?
entries.description: Nobel Prize laureates Demis Hassabis and Paul Nurse join Alison Noble, Chair of the Royal Society Science in the Age of AI Working Group, to discuss how scientists can harness AI tools, and what challenges it might bring about. The post How might AI transform science? appeared first on NobelPrize.org.

entries.title: Plasmon-Enhanced Radioisotope Thermophotovoltaic (PRTPV) Power Generation for Interstellar Missions
entries.description: Keunhan ParkUniversity of Utah This proposal seeks to develop a transformative energy system — the plasmon-enhanced radioisotope Thermophotovoltaic (PRTPV) generator — that significantly surpasses the performance of current radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs) in both specific power and efficiency. Designed to achieve a specific power of 17 W/kg and a thermal-to-electric conversion efficiency greater than 40%, […]

entries.title: NASA Assigns Astronaut Deniz Burnham to First Space Station Mission
entries.description: NASA astronaut Deniz Burnham will embark on her first mission to the International Space Station, serving as an Expedition 76 flight engineer. Burnham will launch aboard the Roscosmos Soyuz MS-30 spacecraft with cosmonauts Dmitri Petelin and Konstantin Borisov. Launch is targeted for March 2027, from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, and the trio will spend […]

entries.title: NASA Awards 2026 Innovative Technology Concepts
entries.description: The NASA Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) program has created 18 new awards to support visionary ideas to improve aerospace technologies in areas ranging from the exploration of the solar system to understanding the universe. The 18 NIAC Phase I awards total $3.2 million. Each award provides up to $175,000 for a nine-month initial investigation. The […]

entries.title: Sizing Up the Sargassum Belt
entries.description: Seaweed composing the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt hit near-record levels in June 2026, with the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of America both reaching all-time highs.

entries.title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams Closes Out Space Station Mission
entries.description: After eight months aboard the International Space Station for his first mission, NASA astronaut Chris Williams is preparing to return to Earth. During his assignment, Williams contributed to research for new cancer treatments, advanced the production of materials to improve computers and electronics, ventured into the vacuum of space to complete two spacewalks, and much […]

entries.title: New Crew Members Welcomed to International Space Station
entries.description: From left, Expedition 74 flight engineers Anna Kikina and Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos, and Anil Menon of NASA pose for a July 18, 2026, photo while holding a cake celebrating their recent arrival aboard the International Space Station. The trio arrived at the space station on July 14, 2026, after launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome […]

entries.title: NASA Joins Genesis Mission to Accelerate AI-Driven Discovery
entries.description: NASA is supporting the Genesis Mission, a national effort to drive the use of artificial intelligence in tackling complex scientific and engineering challenges to advance a new era of discovery. President Donald J. Trump issued the Executive Order “Launching the Genesis Mission” on Nov. 24, 2025, creating a national mission to leverage artificial intelligence to […]

entries.description: Marco QuadrelliNASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Humanity has never touched the particles of a planetary ring, but if we were able to get close enough and sample them, it will transform understanding of ring structure and origins for Saturn (dense), Uranus and Neptune (tenuous), rings of other objects such as Centaurs Chariklo and Chiron, and even early […]

entries.title: NASA to Host Media Briefing on Roman Telescope, Launching Next Month
entries.description: Media are invited to join NASA for a virtual news conference at 2 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, July 29, to preview the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission, scheduled to launch from the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Sunday, Aug. 30. NASA will stream this event live through a variety of platforms. Learn where […]

entries.title: Two new Galileo satellites enter service
entries.description: Two new satellites have now officially joined Europe’s Galileo satellite navigation constellation, strengthening its capabilities, resilience and autonomy. Four Galileo First Generation satellites remain to be launched, with the next pair planned for the end of the year.

entries.title: FLEX and Sentinel-3C arrive at Europe’s Spaceport
entries.description: With liftoff scheduled for September, excitement is building at Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana as two cutting-edge Earth observation satellites, FLEX and Copernicus Sentinel-3C, have arrived to begin their launch campaigns. Over the coming weeks, engineers and mission teams will carry out a series of rigorous inspections and prepare the satellites to be installed atop their Vega-C rocket for their journey into orbit.

entries.title: Look for NASA+ Now Streaming on Amazon Fire TV
entries.description: Continuing agency efforts to bring space closer to home, NASA+ is heading to more streaming platforms. On Thursday, NASA announced its programming is on Fire TV Channels. Fire TV customers can easily access this content by asking Alexa+ on compatible devices. Future programming on Fire TV may include science mission launches, a test flight for […]

entries.title: Robotic Servicing Mission Launches with NASA Support
entries.description: Following its liftoff from Cape Canaveral on July 21 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, the Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV) hosting the NASA-supported Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS) payload is now en route to geosynchronous Earth orbit, where it will use its advanced robotics to service spacecraft. RSGS leverages in-space robotics expertise from NASA, […]

entries.title: NASA to Showcase Agency’s Newest Wind Tunnel in Virginia
entries.description: Media are invited to NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, on Friday, July 31, to attend a media tour and ribbon-cutting ceremony for the Flight Dynamics Research Facility, the agency’s first new wind tunnel in more than 40 years. The event will include a brief media availability with: This event is in person only […]

entries.title: Mapping Alien Continents: Achieving Optical VLBI for Exoplanet Imaging
entries.description: Paul StankusBrookhaven Science Associates The scientific goal of the proposed work will be reconstructing the image, ie resolving surface features, of an Earth-like exoplanet around a nearby star as seen in visible light. The innovation is in two stages. First, the design of a new kind of nulling interferometer — “dynamic hierarchical nulling” — combining inputs […]

entries.title: Robotically Assembled Electromagnetic Metamaterials for Long-Range Space Situational Awareness
entries.description: David SmithDuke University The increasing population of spacefaring vehicles and satellites motivates increasingly powerful technologies for space situational awareness (SSA). While the US space surveillance network (SSN) is able to monitor objects down to about four inches in size using, for example, the latest upgrade to the space fence, the associated requirements limit implementation to ground-based […]

entries.title: Precision Astrometry Using Optically Independent Spacecraft for Graviational Wave Detection
entries.description: Paul StankusBrookhaven Science Associates The scientific goal is to enable a new method for observing gravitational waves at low frequencies, based on the astrometric GW signature — gravitational waves passing by the Earth will cause a (very small) coordinated apparent motion of all sky objects. Our innovation is to deploy a new approach to precision […]

entries.title: A New Compact Instrument Enables High-Fidelity Measurements of Energetic Particles on CubeSats
entries.description: A team of NASA-sponsored scientists and engineers has developed a novel approach to observing high-energy particles in the near-Earth space environment, incorporating miniaturized sensors into a compact, multi-view particle detection instrument unlike any before it. Built for NASA’s Relativistic Electron Atmospheric Loss (REAL) CubeSat mission, the innovative instrument (also called REAL) enables more complete measurements […]

entries.title: From Hampton to Mars: How NASA Langley Helped Land on the Red Planet
entries.description: Fifty years ago, NASA’s Viking 1 and 2 landers made the first successful landings on Mars, opening a new era in planetary exploration. Behind that achievement was a team at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, whose steady leadership and technical expertise helped turn an ambitious idea into a mission that reshaped how we […]

entries.title: NASA Invites Media to Roman Space Telescope, Crew-13 Launches
entries.description: Media accreditation now is open for the launch of NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the agency’s SpaceX Crew-13 missions, both targeting launch in the coming months. The Roman telescope is slated to launch no earlier than 7:20 a.m. EDT Sunday, Aug. 30, aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at […]

entries.title: NASA’s Psyche Mission Images Details of Martian Surface During Flyby
entries.description: Description Captured by the multispectral imager instrument on NASA’s Psyche mission, this is an enhanced-color mosaic created from four individual images acquired on May 15, 2026, during the spacecraft’s flyby of Mars. Psyche was traveling from right to left (northeast to southwest on Mars) during the six minutes that it took to acquire the images for […]

entries.title: Neptune's Inner Moons May Be Shattered Remains of Ancient Icy Worlds
entries.description: In 1989, the Voyager 2 mission discovered six new moons orbiting Neptune, including five tiny ones that orbit just outside the planet's main rings. Because of their small sizes and locations, these satellites have been difficult to study from Earth. Now, using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a team of Caltech researchers has observed Neptune's rings and three of those moons—Larissa, Galatea, and Proteus—and found that their composition is unique among outer solar system bodies.These findings point to the existence of an original moon system that was demolished when Triton, Neptune's

entries.title: Plato's electronics ready for space
entries.description: Image: The European Space Agency’s terrestrial planet hunter Plato has recently completed a series of key tests inside the Maxwell Test Chamber at ESTEC, demonstrating that its electronic equipment is fit to work in space. This photo captures the spacecraft standing inside the special chamber. The shielded enclosure features conducting metal walls, floor, and ceiling that form a Faraday cage, screening out all external interference. Its 9 m-high interior is lined floor to ceiling with foam spikes that absorb electrical signals and sounds to mimic the void of space. Once the chamber was sealed

entries.title: Deep space software upgrade for Hera’s asteroid visit
entries.description: Operating across 140 million km of space, the control team for ESA’s Hera mission have succeeded in upgrading the software running the spacecraft, leaving it ready to explore the distant Dimorphos and Didymos asteroids this autumn.

entries.title: Unpacking Europe’s new weather imagers
entries.description: The second Meteosat Third Generation Imager satellite (MTG-I2) has begun its launch campaign, during which it will go through final inspections before being fitted inside the fairing of the Ariane 6 rocket that will launch it into space towards the end of the summer. So how will this 3800 kg satellite help improve weather forecasts for Europe and North Africa?

entries.title: The most spectacular aurora of the εpsilon mission (so far!)
entries.description: Video: 00:01:17 This timelapse was published on social media by ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot with the following caption: Day 139, orbit 2155 — After the pictures (available in HD on my Flickr account), I'm so happy to finally share the timelapse of the most spectacular aurora of the εpsilon mission so far! Watching this glowing green ribbon shimmer and dance, it's easy to lose yourself completely in the magic of the moment. Turn the sound on for the full experience – the music was carefully chosen to bring you as close as possible to what I felt watching this from space . -- Jour 139, orbite 21

entries.title: New Cohort of KISS Study Programs Push the Frontiers of Space Exploration
entries.description: Five new study topics have been selected by the Keck Institute for Space Studies (KISS) at Caltech to develop collaborations, frameworks, and mission concepts to transform the future of space exploration. The projects were competitively selected as part of KISS's annual cohort from over two dozen proposals.KISS Study Programs focus on developing ideas and concepts that can revolutionize space science and engineering, leveraging Caltech's deep collaborative ties with JPL—which Caltech manages for NASA—and facilitating connections between academia, commercial industry, and government agencies. E

entries.title: Live coverage: SpaceX to launch classified payload for National Reconnaissance Office
entries.description: The NROL-95 mission will be the third payload for the National Reconnaissance Office launched under the National Security Space Launch Phase 2 procurement. Liftoff from pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is scheduled for 3:09 a.m. EDT (0709 UTC).

entries.title: Live coverage: SpaceX ready for 2nd attempt to launch Starship Flight 13 following post-abort engine work
entries.description: The flight comes as Tropical Storm Bertha is expected to make landfall in Texas on Thursday. Liftoff of the Starship Flight 13 mission is scheduled during a 90-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. CDT (6:45 p.m. EDT / 2245 UTC).

entries.title: Live coverage: SpaceX to launch novel geosynchronous robotic servicing satellite on decade-long mission
entries.description: Northrop Grumman’s Mission Robotic Vehicle features the Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS) payload from the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory and DARPA. Liftoff from pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is scheduled during a four-hour window that opens at 5:15 p.m. EDT (2115 UTC).

entries.title: Live coverage: SpaceX tries again to launch Starlink mission from California following abort
entries.description: The Starlink 17-39 mission is SpaceX’s 85th Falcon 9 rocket launch of the year. Liftoff from pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for 7:43 a.m. PDT (10:43 a.m. EDT / 1443 UTC).

entries.title: SpaceX suffers rare, last-second Falcon 9 rocket launch abort
entries.description: The Starlink 17-39 mission is SpaceX’s 85th Falcon 9 rocket launch of the year. Liftoff from pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for 7:49 a.m. PDT (10:49 a.m. EDT / 1449 UTC).

entries.title: Post-ignition anomaly causes abort of SpaceX’s Starship Flight 13
entries.description: The mission will also test out a series of improvements to the launcher to help push it closer to full reusability. Liftoff from pad 2 at Starbase, Texas, was aborted at ignition due to an engine-related issue.

entries.title: SpaceX launches a flight-proven Falcon booster for 600th time
entries.description: The Starlink 10-45 mission added another 29 broadband internet satellites to SpaceX’s low Earth orbit constellation. Liftoff from pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station happened at 5:10 a.m. EDT (0910 UTC).

entries.title: SpaceX launches Falcon 9 rocket on record-breaking 36th flight
entries.description: The flight-leading booster, B1067, launched the Starlink 10-42 mission from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Liftoff from pad 40 happened at 5:25 a.m. EDT (0925 UTC) on Thursday morning.

entries.title: Semiconductor manufacturing test bed flies alongside Starlink satellites on Falcon 9 launch
entries.description: Liftoff of the Starlink 10-50 mission from Space Launch Complex 40 happened at 6:50 a.m. EDT (1050 UTC). The rocket's first-stage booster carried two semiconductor manufacturing pods for Besxar Space Industries.

entries.title: ECLIPSE – Efficient variable Conductivity Lunar Insulator for Passive Surveyor Environmental control
entries.description: Austin Phoenix Virginia Polytechnic Institute & State A disaggregated lunar infrastructure requires novel thermal management methods to enable future lunar operations. While thermal management solutions exist for large infrastructure, the smaller mobile systems that operate independently require improved temperature regulation devices that can survive without heaters or substantial power requirements, while limiting stress-inducing temperature fluctuations. New […]

entries.title: New European exercise device begins testing with first rope-pulling workout in space
entries.description: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot has begun testing the European Enhanced Exploration Exercise Device (E4D) on the International Space Station. Installed inside ESA's Columbus laboratory, the new exercise system will spend the next two years helping researchers evaluate innovative ways to keep astronauts healthy during long-duration space missions.

entries.title: Shape-shifting mirrors on NASA’s new space telescope could unveil Jupiters like our own
entries.description: When NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches, as early as the end of next month, it will attempt one of astronomy’s most precise disappearing acts to date. The telescope will carry the first space-bound “active” coronagraph, an instrument that effectively erases most of the light from a star during photography. It will allow astronomers…

entries.title: Super Heavy-Starship rocket chalks up mostly successful test flight
entries.description: Powered by 33 methane-fueled Raptor engines, the 397-foot-tall two-stage rocket blasted off from SpaceX's "Starbase," Texas, launch site at 5:51 p.m. EDT, putting on a spectacular show for area residents and tourists as it climbed away atop some 16 million pounds of thrust.

entries.title: Critical NASA Deep Space ground station in Spain evacuated due to wildfires
entries.description: The Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex is one of three critical sites around the world that communicate with spacecraft beyond the reach of near-Earth communications capabilities.

entries.title: SpaceX launches 21 communications satellites for the Space Development Agency
entries.description: The Tranche 1 Transporter Layer E (T1TL-E) mission was the third batch of operational satellites launched to support the SDA’s Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture satellite constellation. Liftoff from pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base happened at 1:32 p.m. PDT (4:32 p.m. EDT / 2032 UTC).

entries.title: SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites on Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg
entries.description: The Starlink 15-14 mission will add another 27 broadband internet satellites to the low Earth orbit constellation. Liftoff from pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base happened at 6:28:17 p.m. PDT (9:28:17 p.m. EDT / 0128:17 UTC).

entries.title: Caltech Welcomes Ray Jayawardhana as Tenth President
entries.description: On July 1, 2026, Caltech welcomed renowned astrophysicist, acclaimed author, and transformative leader, Ray Jayawardhana, as the Institute's tenth president, Sonja and William Davidow Presidential Chair, and professor of astronomy."Today, I'm honored to begin my service as Caltech's 10th president," Jayawardhana wrote in his first message to the Caltech community. "Long before this day appeared on the horizon, Caltech and JPL have held a special place in my mind as beacons of humanity's most ambitious acts of exploration and discovery."Jayawardhana joins Caltech with a focus on leading the Ins

entries.title: Architecting a Better Lithium-Ion Battery
entries.description: Since the early 2000s, lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries have become the predominant rechargeable power source for many mobile devices, electric vehicles, renewable-energy storage grids, and more. But the Li-ion batteries in commercial use carry both safety risks and limitations. Julia R. entries.title: How climate change is redrawing the malaria map in Africa
entries.description: A UC Berkeley-led study finds that rising temperatures could increase the malaria risk in southern and East Africa while reducing it where it is most rampant today, as it becomes so hot that even mosquitoes struggle to survive. The post How climate change is redrawing the malaria map in Africa appeared first on Berkeley News.

entries.title: The Download: lasers for nuclear fuel, and organ preservation advances
entries.description: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. How lasers could help provide fuel for nuclear reactors Nuclear power provides about 9% of global electricity today, and that fraction could tick up as countries look to build new reactors.…

entries.title: How lasers could help provide fuel for nuclear reactors
entries.description: Outside the small town of Paducah, Kentucky, a wealth of uranium is locked away in thousands of storage cylinders filled with waste material from a now-closed nuclear enrichment facility. Lasers could help get it out. A company called Global Laser Enrichment (GLE) is looking to reprocess this old material with a new technology called laser…

entries.title: Building the enterprise environment for agentic AI
entries.description: For the enterprise, the promise of agentic AI is much more than just a better chatbot. It is software agents that execute business tasks end-to-end across people, business workflows, data, and systems. The platform best-suited to run agents is built with proper CPU capacity, resilient data access, policy-aware tool use, observability, memory management, and the…

entries.title: Digital Surveillance Reshapes Fishery Enforcement in Indonesia
entries.description: In the eastern Indian Ocean, south of Java in the vast sea stretching toward Australia, a fishing vessel slightly alters its course while operating near the boundary of its authorized fishing ground. Nothing appears unusual on deck. Nets remain in the water. Engines maintain a steady speed. To the crew, it is an ordinary day at sea. Yet hundreds of kilometers above, satellites continuously record the vessel’s position. entries.title: The quest to keep organs alive outside the body
entries.description: This week, I covered a fascinating effort to preserve organs outside the body.
